# Discovery policy

Discovery produces evidence, never replies. Its output is a shortlist of public
conversations with relevance reasons and attributable sources; engagement decisions
and every drafted word belong to a human afterward.

A conversation qualifies only when all four tests pass: it is active now (recency),
the company has documented experience with the specific problem (standing), the
author is genuinely asking or comparing in public (openness), and a canonical public
URL exposes the substance without an account wall (attribution).

Discovery never drafts, queues, or posts a reply; never contacts an author privately;
never scrapes behind authentication; and never admits a candidate for the author's
prominence alone. A relevance reason that cannot cite matching company experience
disqualifies its candidate.

Every shortlist entry records the canonical URL, the author, the observed timestamp,
the one-sentence relevance reason, and the company evidence it leans on.
